title: Signal Garden
exactPrompt: Turn an original electronic rhythm into a living graphic garden. Let bass, bright percussion, and quiet passages produce visibly different movement, with a clear build and release.

creativeExpansion.premise: An illustrated garden grows from sound energy: broad blue leaves respond to bass, coral flowers breathe, and lilac fans and yellow florets react to bright percussion.
creativeExpansion.impression: Playful, tactile, deliberate botanical graphic design rather than a music-player visualization.
creativeExpansion.palette: Warm paper, ink green, cobalt, coral, lemon and lilac.
creativeExpansion.strongestFrame: An asymmetric garden of unequal silhouettes with a large coral flower balanced by blue veined foliage.
creativeExpansion.rhythm: Measured cumulative energy grows the stems. Different frequency bands drive distinct kinds of movement; a central musical quiet passage lets the garden settle before fuller growth and final release.
creativeExpansion.type: No added labels or title cards.
creativeExpansion.assets: Original Canvas geometry and an original synthesized stereo score. No external imagery, fonts or music.
failureConditions: A hidden BPM grid drives motion instead of the decoded audio
Decorative labels compensate for an uninteresting composition

provenance.soundtrack: Original additive/noise synthesis in generate_audio.py using a fixed seed for reproducible asset creation
provenance.analysis: Computed from rendered soundtrack PCM by helpers/motion_audio.py; no score notes or tempo are passed to the scene

generalizationBoundary: The audio analysis is reusable infrastructure. Garden geometry, score composition and aesthetic mappings are example-specific authored choices. Replaying source yields the same frames; repeating the natural-language prompt alone does not guarantee identical art direction.

repairs.observation: Vertical-only scene scaling flattened the emerging flower and leaf silhouettes
repairs.repair: Growth now scales uniformly around the ground anchor, preserving botanical proportions
